hook: One of Apollo 15's three parachutes collapsed on the way home.
narration: One of Apollo 15's parachutes collapsed on the way home.
Three astronauts were ending a twelve-day Moon landing mission.
Two of them had driven the first car on the Moon, and its camera filmed them blasting off.
Burning thruster fuel ate through its lines. It streamed at a fifth of its normal pull.
[short pause] Apollo was built to land on two chutes. It just hit harder.
outcome: Apollo 15 hit the Pacific hard but safely, and all three astronauts were recovered.

location_card.place: Pacific Ocean, 330 miles north of Honolulu

title: Apollo 15 splashed down on two chutes
description:
One of Apollo 15's three main parachutes collapsed during the descent to the Pacific Ocean on Aug. 7, 1971, after burning thruster fuel damaged its risers. The capsule landed hard on two chutes and the crew was recovered safely.

Footage: NASA video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/Apollo%2015%20Never%20Been%20on%20a%20Ride%20like%20this%20Before

facts.claim: Fuel burned through the risers of one chute, which streamed at about a fifth of capacity
facts.source_quote: During re-entry the burning reaction control system fuel burned through the risers of one of the shoots, and that shoot streamed and effectively became about one fifth of its normal capacity.

facts.claim: Designed to land on two chutes; hard but safe landing
facts.source_quote: Apollo 15 landed on two shoots. It was designed to do that, but it did mean a hard landing, but a safe landing.

facts.source_quote: The Lunar Rover had a TV camera on it, and for the first time we were privileged to see the asset stage take off from the moon.

facts.claim: Splashdown Aug. 7, 1971, 330 miles north of Honolulu; one main chute collapsed; Okinawa recovered the crew
facts.source_quote: One of the three main parachutes collapsed during the descent, but did not harm the astronauts.

extra_sources.excerpt: On Aug. 7, 1971, Apollo 15 astronauts David R. Scott, Alfred M. Worden and James B. Irwin ended their successful 12-day Moon landing mission with a splashdown in their Command Module (CM) Endeavour in the Pacific Ocean. The splashdown point 330 miles north of Honolulu was 1 mile from the target and about 6 miles from the prime recovery ship U.S.S. Okinawa (LPH-3). ... One of the three main parachutes collapsed during the descent, but did not harm the astronauts. ... Recovery forces from the U.S.S. Okinawa monitored the descent and landing and retrieved the astronauts and their spacecraft.
